supporting: text, email, radio, checkbox, textarea, submit button

claims.claim: A web form contains controls with which a user supplies data that can be sent to a server for processing.
A label identifies a form control; a label can contain its control or refer to a labelable control with its for attribute and the control's id.
The name attribute supplies the name under which a successful form control's value is submitted; radio buttons with a common name act as a group.
A form action identifies the service URL for a submission and method selects a submission method; GET and POST are common methods.
fieldset groups related controls and legend gives that group a caption, helping users understand related choices.
Browser-side checks can improve feedback but a server must still verify submitted input because a hostile user can bypass client-side validation.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft was generic boilerplate without sources, so it was replaced.
correctionsNeeded: Defined a form as a data-collection and submission interface rather than a generic web concept.
Separated the browser interface from the server's handling of submitted data.
Added explicit labels, grouped choices, and names as basic accessible, interoperable markup.
rightsIssues: WHATWG, MDN, and W3C WAI were used as reference-only sources. All lesson wording is original synthesis.
